subject: Jurisdictional documentation pack & KMS verification for private deployment
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@helixtx.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Procurement <procure@helixtx.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: jurisdictional docs + KMS verification for private deploy

Hi Priyom,

We're starting legal/procurement review for the pilot private deployment and need a compact packet that confirms the following before we move to signature:

- Which physical regions/nodes will host Helix workloads (US/EU/APAC) and the default failover behavior.
- KMS boundary and key custody model for private deployments (do you support HSM-backed keys or BYOK via customer KMS?).
- SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ pointers we can attach to our security team review (specific pages or exported answers are ideal).
- Networking: private peering options, egress control, and per-tenant routing guarantees.

Can you provide a single "jurisdictional pack" (PDF) plus a short KMS verification note we can hand to our infra team? If you can include a one-page network boundary diagram that would be perfect.

Target is to have materials by end of week so procurement can move to DocuSign early next week. Thanks —

Sara Miller
Head of IT Operations
Helix Therapeutics

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Ben (Solutions/Infra) so we can put together the exact artifacts and the short technical verification you requested.

Planned deliverables by EOD Friday (2025-06-13):
- Jurisdictional pack (PDF): node footprint by region, failover & routing model, and a short statement on residency guarantees.
- KMS verification note: custody model, supported integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, HSM options), and suggested key rotation cadence.
- One-page network boundary diagram (PDF).
- SIG/CAIQ pointers and an export of relevant SIG answers (zipped).

Ben will confirm a few technical details (HSM vs Redwood-managed keys) and we may ask for a quick network diagram from Helix to confirm peering details.

Attaching a delivery timeline and checklist so you can see what we'll hand off.

Thanks —
Priyom Das

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Sara Miller <sara.miller@helixtx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: jurisdictional docs + KMS verification for private deploy

Sara / team — quick technical clarifications from infra so we produce the right KMS note:

1) Key custody options we can verify:
   - Redwood-managed keys (default): keys stored in our HSM cluster; customer data encrypted at rest. We retain key lifecycle operations but provide audit logs and can rotate on an agreed cadence.
   - Customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK): we support AWS KMS and GCP CMEK integrations; customers upload key material or provide key ARNs; Redwood never exports the plaintext key.
   - HSM-backed on-prem option: for fully air-gapped/private installs we can run customer HSMs and provide a verified key handshake process (requires coordination with your crypto team).

2) For the network diagram: we need a minimal topology showing your on-prem/VPC CIDR ranges and whether you'll use a private peering or VPN tunnel. If you can send that as a simple Visio/PNG we'll align our boundary diagram.

3) Attestation level for SIG/CAIQ: we can provide a SIG export and mark each control "applicable/not applicable" with references to our SOC 2 report where relevant. We can't alter SIG answers per-customer but will include the latest exported copy.

I'll attach the KMS key rotation flow and a sample network boundary we propose. Also note that for procurement language we can add a short clause describing failover behavior (active-active in-region by default; cross-region failover is opt-in with documented RPO/RTO).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: kms_key_rotation_flow.png (stub); network_boundary_diagram.pdf (stub)
From: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@helixtx.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Procurement <procure@helixtx.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: jurisdictional docs + KMS verification for private deploy

Thanks Ben — that helps. I've attached a minimal network topology (helix_network_topology.vsdx) showing our VPC CIDRs and the subnets we'd like to peer. A couple of notes / asks from my side:

- For CMEK/BYOK, can you confirm whether Redwood will ever have ability to sign/rotate the key? We need an explicit "no export, no rotate without customer approval" statement for our security team.
- For HSM-backed private installs: what is the expected lead time and any specific vendor support requirements (Thales/Entrust/YubiHSM etc.)?
- We also need the SIG export and a pointer to the SOC 2 report pages that reference key management and network segmentation. Can you include the exact page numbers in the pack?

If you can get the jurisdictional pack and KMS note to us by Friday EOD that would let procurement proceed on Monday (we've penciled in the DocuSign workflow for 6/16).

Tom Nguyen
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Helix Therapeutics
+t.nguyen@helixtx.com
